warmup.description: Gently connect breath to core activation and mobilize the spine.
movements: Supine diaphragmatic breathing x 6 slow breaths

main_exercises.name: Spine articulation flow
main_exercises.form_cue: Move one vertebra at a time, lifting and lowering with control and breath.

main_exercises.name: Deep core activation (dead bug variations)
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep lower back gently anchored as limbs move slowly and deliberately.

main_exercises.name: Side-lying oblique engagement
main_exercises.form_cue: Lift through the waist rather than pushing from the shoulder or legs.

main_exercises.name: Front body length and control (modified plank holds)
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep a long line from head to heels, maintaining gentle core engagement.

main_exercises.name: Seated rotation and control
main_exercises.form_cue: Rotate from the ribcage while keeping hips grounded and stable.

cooldown.description: Release tension and encourage relaxation through breath and gentle stretching.
movements: Child’s pose with slow breathing x 90s

phase_notes.menstrual: This gentle, breath-focused session is well-suited here—move slowly and prioritize comfort, especially in spine articulation work.
phase_notes.follicular: Use this session to refine control and connection—slightly increase precision and range of motion where it feels good.
phase_notes.ovulatory: You may feel more mobile and stable—explore slightly longer holds or deeper engagement while maintaining smooth, controlled movement.
phase_notes.early_luteal: A great session to maintain consistency—focus on steady pacing and clean transitions between movements.
phase_notes.late_luteal: Lean into the calming nature of this session—prioritize breath, reduce range if needed, and focus on gentle core engagement.
